title: Composition law for per-variable restriction weights
statement:
Regard each coordinate of a random restriction as being in one of three states: *free* (written $\ast$) or *fixed* to one of the two Boolean values. For a parameter $p \in \bbr$, let $w_p$ be the per-variable weight assigning $w_p(\ast) = p$ to the free state and $(1-p)/2$ to each of the two fixed states, and define the composite $a \circ b$ of two states to equal $a$ when $a$ is fixed and $b$ when $a$ is free. Then for all $p, q \in \bbr$ and every state $c$,
\[
  \sum_{a}\sum_{b} w_p(a)\, w_q(b)\, [\,a \circ b = c\,] = w_{pq}(c),
\]
where both sums range over the three states and $[\,\cdot\,]$ equals $1$ when the enclosed equation holds and $0$ otherwise.
replaced:
For parameters $p, q \in \bbr$ and any outcome $c$, summing the products
$\mathrm{varWeight}\,p\,a \cdot \mathrm{varWeight}\,q\,b$ over all pairs $(a,b)$ whose
composition equals $c$ gives $\mathrm{varWeight}\,(pq)\,c$:
\[
  \sum_{a} \sum_{b} \mathrm{varWeight}\,p\,a \cdot \mathrm{varWeight}\,q\,b \cdot
    [\,a \,\triangleright\, b = c\,] = \mathrm{varWeight}\,(pq)\,c.
\]
